scenario.title: BELGRADE OFFENSIVE - 12 OCT 1944
intro.text:
BELGRADE OFFENSIVE - 12 OCT 1944

West of Belgrade, Serbia

The time has come to liberate the Serbian capital from the fascist bondage! With the support of the Yugoslav Partisans and the Bulgarian Army, it should not be difficult to drive out the Germans and their collaborators.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The ring at Iași closed before the Sixth Army understood which roads had become walls. Romania's political position changed almost as quickly as the front.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-victory.text: The Iași–Chișinău operation broke the front and trapped the main force. The pursuit is already crossing borders the old situation map treated as permanent.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-tactical.text: The pocket closed, though its western seams leaked men and vehicles. The military result is decisive; the political consequences are moving faster still.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-a.text: At Iași you turned inward and helped close the ring. The result made coordination look inevitable after the fact; three armies remember how many liaison calls it actually required.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The crossings seized beyond Iași kept the pursuit moving after the pocket closed behind us. Some infantry commanders still say the mobile group left them to finish another man's battle.
line.scene-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-0.text: Three liaison teams stand around one map and use three sets of place names. The Partisan officer knows tracks absent from every printed sheet; the Bulgarian staff knows when its artillery can move; our timetable knows only the hour.
line.scene-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.scene-1.text: One command would simplify my fire plan. It would also ask men who fought here for three years to follow roads chosen by officers who arrived this week.
line.decision.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.decision.text: We can impose one central axis and reduce confusion, or divide sectors according to local knowledge and accept that the assault will not look tidy from headquarters.
Give each allied force a defined sector and build the timetable around local routes.
Give infantry and reconnaissance formations 20 experience each and gain 80 prestige from effective coalition cooperation.
line.decision.choice.single-command-axis: Concentrate the heavy forces on one axis under a single fire plan.
Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give artillery 25 experience; centralised preparations cost 40 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-0.text: Partisan guides lead the routes they know, Bulgarian guns support the sector assigned to them, and our mobile group exploits between both. Liaison officers carry authority, not merely messages.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-1.text: Separate sectors need one artillery boundary and one word that stops a pursuit. Agree those with the Partisan and Bulgarian officers before our first shell crosses either line.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-0.text: The central axis gets every heavy gun and one traffic plan. Allied detachments secure the flanks without being pulled into a battle they were not briefed to fight.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-1.text: A single axis is easier for us and asks our allies to become flank guards in their own capital. I will carry the order. I will not call their resentment confusion.
line.post-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.post-0.text: Belgrade is a capital and a living city, not a coloured objective. Coordination must reduce both delay and destruction.
